sources.entry: Hangar - Menu bar launcher for one-click, toggleable terminal and app snippets.

summary.one_liner: Hangar is a lightweight native macOS menu bar app that turns terminal commands and app launches into one-click, toggleable snippets.
summary.what_it_does: Hangar sits in the macOS menu bar and keeps a compact list of pinned workflows. Each terminal snippet opens iTerm2 or Terminal and runs a command when toggled on, and closes the window when toggled off. Command snippets can contain {{name}} placeholders that Hangar prompts for at launch, with a live preview, remembering the last values used. Application snippets launch an app, optionally opening a specific project or file with it. Snippets can be organized into groups with dividers, and a whole group can be flipped with one toggle. Snippets marked for auto-start come back automatically after login.
use_cases: keep long-running build or watch commands visible in the menu bar
start a set of dev workflows automatically after login
toggle a terminal command on and off without re-typing it
launch an IDE with a specific project folder
run parameterized shell commands with prompted values
group related workflows and switch them together
how_to_run: Or download Hangar.dmg from the Releases page and drag Hangar into Applications
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Hangar.app (optional, skips the unverified-developer prompt)
notable: Drives real iTerm2 or Terminal windows via AppleScript, so your own profile, fonts and scrollback apply
Live running indicator that notices when a window is closed manually
Command parameters with {{name}} placeholders, live preview, and remembered answers
Native Swift/AppKit with no Electron and no dock icon
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ and Xcode 15+ to build from source
Ad-hoc signed, not notarized, so first launch needs a manual Gatekeeper override
Needs macOS Automation permission to control the terminal
